**Finding submitted: deviation (ASSIGN), high severity.**

**What I reviewed**
- **§22.4 (p0289)** — the operative assignment clause.
- **§21.11 / 21.11.B (p0281, p0284)** — future acquisitions and Change in Control of Customer.
- **§11 (p0186–p0192)** and the redacted **11.3 "Following Change in Control of Customer"** — no vendor termination right on our change of control; 11.1 excludes 11.3 from the convenience fee, so 11.3 reads as a Customer-side right.
- **"Change in Control" definition (p0028)**.

**Why it deviates**
§22.4 is mutual on its face but asymmetric in substance. M&I may *freely* assign on a merger, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, stock or securities, plus to any successor to its Data Services division. Our carve-out is limited to a merger, and only where the surviving corporation becomes an Affiliate of a financial institution with at least $100,000,000 of capital and surplus — with no affiliate carve-out and no asset-sale carve-out. An internal reorganisation or a sale of substantially all assets would therefore need M&I's consent. That fails the fallback's "mutual right to assign to successors."

**Redline (validated, ok:true)** — mirrors M&I's own carve-out into limb (a): assignment to an Affiliate of Customer or pursuant to a merger, acquisition, corporate reorganization or sale of all or substantially all assets/stock/securities, retaining the Section 21.11 conditions to minimise friction.

**Noted, not redlined:** there is no vendor termination or re-pricing right on our change of control (21.11.B obliges M&I to continue Services), though it caps post-change volumes at the prior three months plus 25% — flagged in the rationale rather than treated as a separate breach.
